claim: Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve sits 3 miles north of Guerneville on Armstrong Woods Road, charges $10 per vehicle ($9 seniors), is free to pedestrians and cyclists, and protects old-growth coast redwoods.
quote: Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve allows visitors to experience the beauty of the coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens).

claim: Armstrong Redwoods has 9.2 miles of trails; the Pioneer Nature Trail is a 1.5-mile round-trip, mostly flat and ADA-accessible, and limited free parking is available along Armstrong Woods Road or by walking in from the entrance lot.
quote: Admission is $10 per vehicle, $9 per vehicle for seniors and free to pedestrians and cyclists. Limited free parking is available along Armstrong Redwoods Road on the west side of the road only.

claim: Lake Sonoma is a 17,615-acre park 13 miles northwest of Healdsburg with more than 40 miles of trails for hikers, equestrians and mountain bikers, plus boating, swimming, fishing, a disc golf course and a year-round Visitor Center and Fish Hatchery.
quote: More than 40 miles of trails welcome hikers, horseback riders and mountain bikers to Lake Sonoma, a 17,615 acre park 13 miles northwest of Healdsburg.

claim: Lake Sonoma trail options include the Woodland Ridge Nature Trail with Dry Creek Valley views, the moderate 4.3-mile Dry Creek and Bummer Trail Loop, and the challenging North Slope to Bummer Peak Loop.
quote: The moderate 4.3-mile Dry Creek and Bummer Trail Loop, featuring varied terrain and panoramic views.

claim: Riverfront Regional Park (7821 Eastside Road, Healdsburg) offers 3.12 miles of trails including the 2.18-mile Lake Trail around Lake Benoist and a half-mile Redwood Hill Trail through a coast redwood grove; dogs allowed on leash; parking $8 fall/winter/spring and $12 summer; open 7am to sunset.
quote: The park offers 3.12 miles of trails total. The main Lake Trail spans 2.18 miles and circles Lake Benoist, while the Redwood Hill Trail covers half a mile through a coastal redwood forest.

claim: Healdsburg Ridge Open Space Preserve is 155 acres of oak woodlands, wetlands, serpentine chaparral and grasslands with roughly 2-3 miles of easy-to-moderate trails, dogs allowed on leash, but only residential street parking and no restrooms.
quote: Healdsburg Ridge Open Space Preserve is 155 acres of oak woodlands, wetlands, rocky serpentine chaparral, and open grasslands.

claim: Foothill Regional Park (1351 Arata Lane, Windsor) is 211 acres with nearly 7 miles of multi-use trails ranging from the challenging Alta Vista Trail to the wheelchair-accessible Three Lakes Trail, three fishing ponds, $8 parking, and dogs allowed on leash.
quote: The park maintains nearly 7 miles of pathways. Trail options range from challenging terrain like Alta Vista Trail to easier routes such as the Three Lakes Trail, which is wheelchair-accessible.

claim: Shiloh Ranch Regional Park (5750 Faught Road, Windsor) is an 850-acre Mayacamas-foothills park with nearly 8 miles of moderate looped multi-use trails and $8 parking, but dogs are prohibited on trails (allowed only in picnic areas and parking lot).
quote: Nearly 8 miles of looped trails accommodate hiking, biking, and horseback riding... Dogs on leash are prohibited from trails but permitted in picnic areas and the parking lot.
